options.B: It drives them to refuse all forms of parenteral therapy
options.C: It makes them prioritize fast relief over questioning safety practices
options.D: It encourages them to thoroughly inspect every single medical package

explanation: Spot on! When someone just wants to get well and get back to their daily hustle, safety checks take a back seat.

question: When is the very first (baseline) needle count done during a procedure?

options.A: When the patient is rolling out of the recovery room
options.B: After the surgeon has closed the skin incision
options.C: Before the surgery begins during instrument setup
options.D: Only when an emergency X-ray is requested

explanation: Fantastic! We always do a baseline count before any cut is made so we know exactly what we started with. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: Which type of FGM involves narrowing the vaginal opening and creating a seal?

options.A: Type III

question: What is a common consequence of poor communication during the implementation phase?

options.A: Immediate dismissal of the local village traditional ruler

options.D: Instant failure of government financial auditing systems

question: You are caring for a 38-week pregnant mother with many past deliveries who also has severe anemia. What is the best delivery recommendation?

options.A: Advise delivery at a well-equipped hospital that has blood transfusion services.
options.B: Wait for spontaneous labor at home until contractions are very close.
options.C: Plan a home birth attended by a traditional birth attendant.
options.D: Encourage unassisted labor to avoid medical interventions.

explanation: Because she has a high risk of heavy bleeding and low blood count, she needs to deliver where doctors and nurses can easily give blood or emergency care.

question: What daily habit is most important for a patient with heart failure to spot early fluid buildup?

options.A: Testing their blood sugar levels
options.B: Checking their pulse every hour
options.C: Weighing themselves daily
options.D: Measuring their daily urine output

explanation: Spot on! A sudden jump on the scale is often the very first warning sign that the body is retaining fluid, so a daily weigh-in is a lifesaver.

question: What is typically the earliest symptom experienced by someone developing an occupational lung disease?

options.A: A persistent cough and shortness of breath with exertion
options.B: Sudden paralysis of both lower extremities
options.C: Complete loss of the sense of taste and smell
options.D: Bright yellow coloration of the skin and eyes

explanation: Early lung damage usually manifests as a mild, dry cough and breathlessness that only appears when the person engages in physical work or exercise. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why does primary health care place heavy emphasis on nutrition and safe water alongside medical treatment?

options.A: Nurses are trained as civil engineers rather than clinicians
options.B: Preventing disease through basic sanitation stops sickness before it starts
options.C: Doctors refuse to treat patients who do not drink boiled water
options.D: Water and food are more profitable than pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Clean water and good nutrition address the root environmental causes of infection, reducing the burden on clinics. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)

question: What usually happens when a hospital's stated values do not match how its leaders actually behave?

options.A: Trust dissolves rapidly among staff and stakeholders
options.B: The organization immediately goes bankrupt by law

options.D: Employees begin working harder to compensate for leaders

explanation: When leaders say one thing and do another, hypocrisy kills workplace trust and staff morale very quickly.

question: Why can a man still cause a pregnancy right after getting a vasectomy?

options.B: The body continues to produce live sperm inside the vas deferens tubes
options.C: Sperm already stored above the surgical cut remain active for weeks

question: What is considered the single most effective method to prevent the spread of infections in a clinical setting?

options.A: Routine room painting
options.B: Proper hand hygiene

options.D: Administering vitamins

explanation: Regular and thorough hand washing or sanitizing removes transient microorganisms acquired from touching patients and contaminated surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h4)

question: What happens during the process of clot retraction?

options.A: White blood cells destroy excess fibrinogen in the plasma

options.C: The blood pressure drops to prevent further vessel damage
options.D: Red blood cells multiply to replace the lost fluid volume

question: What skill helps a leader look past surface drama and find the real root cause of a ward problem?

options.A: Speed reading

options.C: Critical thinking
options.D: Public speaking

explanation: Critical thinking is your detective tool. It helps you dig beneath surface complaints to figure out what is actually causing the trouble on the ward.

question: A patient with kidney disease is given a standard dose of a drug that leaves the body through the kidneys. As a nurse, what is your best action?

question: If a nurse wants to reach tech-savvy urban youth to talk about waste management, what is the best channel?

options.A: Printed paper leaflets
options.B: Medical textbooks

options.D: Social media

question: Which nursing action provides the most accurate daily measurement of fluid retention in a hospitalized patient?

options.A: Asking the patient how tight their shoes feel each morning

question: What kind of practical help can faith-based communities offer to people with physical disabilities?

options.A: Official legal representation in medical malpractice lawsuits

options.C: Volunteer networks and accessible transportation assistance
options.D: Advanced surgical interventions and prescription drug manufacturing

question: How do school health programs help students do better in their studies?

options.A: By guaranteeing admission to higher education
options.B: By replacing traditional classroom teaching hours
options.C: By eliminating the need for private tutoring
options.D: By reducing absences caused by preventable illnesses

question: What is another common medical name for hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Community outbreaks
options.B: Endogenous illnesses
options.C: Pathological infections
options.D: Nosocomial infections

explanation: Great recall! Nosocomial infections are simply illnesses that patients pick up while receiving care inside a hospital or clinic.

question: When the kidneys secrete hydrogen ions into the urine, what vital body balance are they maintaining?

options.A: Red blood cell production
options.B: Calcium and bone density
options.C: Acid-base balance
options.D: Blood glucose balance

question: What is the main difference between blood plasma and serum?

options.A: Plasma is found outside blood vessels while serum is found inside

options.C: Serum lacks clotting proteins like fibrinogen because it has already clotted

question: What is the main job of the epiglottis when you swallow food?

options.A: To produce sound through the vocal cords
options.B: To filter dust particles out of the nose
options.C: To warm and humidify incoming air
options.D: To cover the windpipe and prevent food from entering the lungs

explanation: Think of the epiglottis as a tiny trapdoor. When you swallow, it folds down over your windpipe so your food and drink safely slide down the esophagus instead of going into your lungs!

question: A patient asks how regular exercise helps prevent infections. What is the best way to answer?

options.A: It improves blood circulation so immune cells move more efficiently through your body.
options.B: It replaces the need for getting enough sleep at night.
options.C: It completely stops bacteria from entering your skin.
options.D: It doubles your red blood cell count instantly.

explanation: You got it! Good circulation helps your immune cells patrol the body smoothly and tackle germs faster.

question: Your patient just woke up from surgery and feels dizzy. What should you do about getting them out of bed?

options.A: Use a standard sliding board without help
options.B: Ask the patient to walk alone to test their strength

question: Which imaging test uses a special dye to check if the Fallopian tubes are open?

question: Why do many survivors of FGM experience chronic sexual dysfunction and pain?

question: Why do hospitals in resource-limited settings often start unit dispensing in high-risk units first?

options.B: To comply with international rules regarding surgical theatres only
options.C: To hide implementation failures from hospital management boards

question: Which ion movement mainly causes depolarization when an action potential fires?

question: When does the liver start producing ketone bodies?

options.A: When glucose is unavailable and fats are broken down for fuel

options.D: During heavy weightlifting exercise using arm muscles

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to avoid using leftover antibiotics for a new cold?

options.A: Colds are usually caused by viruses, which antibiotics cannot kill
options.B: Using leftover drugs can lead to incorrect dosing and drug resistance
options.C: Leftover antibiotics are guaranteed to work faster than fresh prescriptions

question: A client is charting her basal body temperature (BBT). What is the key thing she must know about this method?

question: Into how many main categories does the World Health Organization divide FGM?

question: Your patient starts having trouble breathing and facial swelling right after a new IV antibiotic starts. What should you do first?

question: What is a crucial first step when caring for a malnourished child who also has an acute infection?

options.C: Discharge the child immediately for home management

question: What is the primary focus of organisational objectives in healthcare?

question: What long-term heart problem often develops from chronic, untreated severe anemia?

question: What is a major ethical puzzle that community health nurses face more often than hospital nurses?

question: What happens in the condition known as vasa praevia?

question: What stops your windpipe (trachea) from squishing or collapsing when you breathe?

question: A clinic ensures that its facility can be reached easily by rural women and has fair pricing. Which core dimension is being prioritized?

question: Which practice is strictly forbidden when handling chemicals in any hospital or lab setting?

question: A newborn has a persistent shunt directing blood from the pulmonary artery to the aorta. What structure failed to manage this normal foetal pathway?

question: What is the primary goal of geriatric home healthcare?

question: You are serving lunch to a patient who is legally blind. What is the best way to help them eat independently?

question: What is a common misunderstanding about the role of the triage nurse?

question: What is the main purpose of tracking indicators in a PAC monitoring and evaluation system?

options.A: To publicly expose staff members who make clinical mistakes

question: A stroke patient is having trouble swallowing food safely and speaks with slurred words. Who should you call first?

question: Why do many couples in local communities prefer traditional family planning methods?

question: What is the normal adult blood range for potassium?

options.C: 22 to 29 mmol/L
options.D: 135 to 145 mmol/L

explanation: Potassium must stay within a tight range of 3.5 to 5.0 mmol/L to keep the heart beating regularly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which post-sigmoidoscopy symptom means a patient might have a bowel perforation and needs emergency care?

options.A: Suddenly feeling very sleepy and tired
options.B: Passing frequent gas in the first couple of hours
options.C: Sudden, severe worsening belly pain with a hard, rigid stomach
options.D: Finding a tiny streak of bright red blood on the toilet paper once

explanation: Good catch! A rigid, intensely painful belly is a major red flag for a bowel tear (perforation) and needs immediate medical attention.

question: What waste product does the liver make when processing extra amino acids?

options.A: Lactic acid
options.B: Bile salt
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Urea

explanation: The liver takes toxic ammonia from protein breakdown and turns it into safer urea so your kidneys can easily flush it out.

question: Which of these best describes the 'total pain' concept?

options.A: Spiritual pain cannot be assessed by healthcare workers
options.B: Pain is caused entirely by physical tissue destruction
options.C: Physical pain is worsened by emotional, social, and spiritual distress
options.D: Pain medications are the only effective treatment for suffering

explanation: Total pain reminds us that when a patient is worried, lonely, or spiritually troubled, their physical pain often hurts even more. Everything is connected!

question: What is the primary function of the respiratory system that gets disrupted during disorders?

options.A: Nutrient absorption
options.B: Blood filtration
options.C: Fluid balance control
options.D: Gas exchange

explanation: The main job of the respiratory system is moving oxygen into the blood and removing carbon dioxide. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h1)

question: What percentage range of an adolescent's daily calories should ideally come from carbohydrates?
explanation: Carbohydrates provide the primary fuel source for daily energy and should form the largest share of teen calorie intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h2)

question: What is the main reason we help patients work on their range of motion during rehab?

options.A: To increase the resting blood pressure of the client
options.B: To permanently numb the nerves surrounding a painful joint
options.C: To double the physical size of damaged muscle fibers
options.D: To prevent joint contractures and keep tissues flexible

explanation: Spot on! Moving those joints gently stops them from freezing up or getting stiff so the patient can keep their flexibility.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common consequence of relying solely on a free market for healthcare?

options.A: Universal and equal access for all citizens regardless of wealth
options.B: Neglect of unprofitable public health services
options.C: Lack of basic care for uninsured populations
options.D: Geographic concentration of hospitals in wealthy urban areas

explanation: A pure free market distributes care based on ability to pay, which naturally creates disparities rather than universal equal access. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the medical term for when a child starts going through puberty much earlier than normal?

options.A: Hypogonadism
options.B: Precocious puberty
options.C: Acromegaly
options.D: Delayed puberty

explanation: Great job! 'Precocious' means developing certain talents or traits earlier than expected—in this case, early puberty.

question: Why is strict bed rest ordered during the early, active phase of myocarditis?

options.A: To lower the workload on the inflamed heart muscle
options.B: To stop blood clots from forming in the legs
options.C: To stop the kidneys from making too much urine
options.D: To keep the patient's blood pressure high

explanation: Resting lowers the heart rate and reduces the amount of work the heart has to do, giving the sore muscle time to heal. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which wearable device is best for continuous, medical-grade heart rhythm monitoring?

options.A: A standard consumer fitness wristband
options.B: A basic smartphone pedometer app
options.C: An adhesive medical-grade patch
options.D: A smart textile running t-shirt

explanation: Medical patches stick securely and are specifically designed to catch every beat of critical heart rhythms accurately.

question: Which observational tool is best used to grade the quality or frequency of a specific behavior?

options.A: Simple checklist
options.B: Consent form
options.C: Rating scale
options.D: Archival record

explanation: Think of a rating scale as a grading tool. It lets you measure the degree or quality of an action, rather than just noting if it happened or not.

question: Which type of vaccine uses a weakened (but still alive) version of a germ?

options.A: Inactivated vaccine
options.B: Subunit vaccine
options.C: Live attenuated vaccine
options.D: Toxoid vaccine

explanation: Well done! 'Attenuated' just means weakened. It gently trains your immune system without causing severe sickness.

question: What is a key sign that a post-abortion patient might be in severe pain?

options.A: Drop in body temperature below normal
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin sclera
options.C: Increased heart rate and breathing rate
options.D: Sudden swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: When someone is in acute pain, their body's natural fight-or-flight response kicks in, causing their heart rate and breathing to speed up. Brilliant nursing observation!

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in home care?

options.A: Spraying household furniture with industrial bleach daily
options.B: Keeping all windows tightly closed during visits
options.C: Performing proper and frequent hand hygiene
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gowns for every home visit

explanation: Good old handwashing and using alcohol rubs remove germs fast, protecting both you and your patient from cross-contamination.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended practice when educating patients about safe medication use?

options.A: Asking a healthcare provider when unsure about a medication change
options.B: Purchasing medicines exclusively from licensed and verified retail pharmacies
options.C: Buying prescription drugs from informal open-air street markets for lower prices
options.D: Checking prescription labels carefully to understand both generic and brand names

explanation: Never encourage buying drugs from street hawkers or open markets! Always guide patients to licensed pharmacies to avoid fake or degraded medications.

question: Which type of nerve signals tell the bladder muscle to squeeze when it's time to pass urine?

options.A: Parasympathetic fibers
options.B: Sympathetic fibers
options.C: Enteric nerve fibers
options.D: Somatic sensory fibers

explanation: When you are ready to use the restroom, parasympathetic nerves from your lower spinal cord kick in to contract your bladder wall (the detrusor muscle) and let urine out.

question: How do clinic registers help nurses identify children who have defaulted?

options.A: By calculating the exact weight the child will gain next month
options.B: By predicting which family will move to another state
options.C: By automatically ordering new vaccine vials from the depot
options.D: By tracking missed return dates between scheduled clinic visits

explanation: Facility registers record attendance dates, making it easy to see when a child fails to return for their next scheduled dose. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h3)

question: Which of these is a common body trigger that can cause a seizure?

options.A: High iron levels
options.B: Excess vitamin C
options.C: Low blood sugar
options.D: Low dietary fiber

explanation: Correct! When blood sugar drops too low (hypoglycemia), brain cells are robbed of their fuel and can trigger a seizure.

question: Why is the chain of infection a helpful tool for nurses?

options.A: It determines the financial cost of treating an infectious outbreak
options.B: It proves whether an infection is bacterial or viral in origin
options.C: It shows where interventions can break the cycle and stop transmission
options.D: It helps nurses calculate the exact incubation period of a virus

explanation: Exactly! By seeing how the links connect, you know exactly where to step in with handwashing or vaccines to stop the spread.

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment during the early and middle stages of this disease?

options.A: Completely curing the underlying genetic defect
options.B: Slowing disease progression and managing blood pressure
options.C: Regenerating completely healthy new kidney tissue
options.D: Stopping all urine production to rest the body

explanation: Since kidney scarring cannot be undone, the primary goal of treatment is to protect the nephrons we have left and keep the patient stable for as long as possible.

question: What helpful role do the resident bacteria in your colon play?

options.A: Digesting the majority of dietary fats and proteins
options.B: Producing protective mucus for the rectal lining
options.C: Synthesizing certain vitamins and fermenting fiber
options.D: Preventing all water absorption to keep stool soft

explanation: Correct! Our gut bacteria are friendly helpers that break down fiber and even manufacture important nutrients like vitamin K for us.

question: Which health problem is most often caused by poor ergonomic design at work?

options.A: Sudden bacterial pneumonia
options.B: Hereditary blood disorders and sickle cell crises
options.C: Musculoskeletal disorders and chronic back pain
options.D: Acute viral gastroenteritis and food poisoning

explanation: Well done! Bad chairs and poorly arranged desks force awkward postures, leading directly to backaches and muscle strains.

question: Why are congregate living settings like nursing homes particularly vulnerable to disease outbreaks?

options.A: The complete absence of handwashing sinks
options.B: The high rate of sudden resident discharges
options.C: The requirement for outdoor recreational sports
options.D: The close proximity of medically frail residents

explanation: Correct! When vulnerable people live close together, germs can spread fast unless we are super strict with our infection control.

question: What are the three core things the TNM staging system looks at?

options.A: Temperature, Nutrition level, and Medication history
options.B: Time of onset, Number of lumps, and Medical history
options.C: Total blood count, Nerve damage, and Muscle tone
options.D: Tumor size, Node involvement, and Metastasis

explanation: T = Tumor size, N = Node spread, M = Metastasis (spread to distant organs). You'll use this staging system all through clinicals!

question: What is the medical term for the very first menstrual period in a young female?

options.A: Amenorrhea
options.B: Menarche
options.C: Menopause
options.D: Dysmenorrhea

explanation: Menarche is the term used to describe the onset of the first menstrual cycle during puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h1)

question: When you have several nursing diagnoses at once, which one should you tackle first?

options.A: Risk for impaired skin integrity on the left heel
options.B: Knowledge deficit regarding a new low-salt diet
options.C: Mild anxiety regarding the upcoming hospital discharge
options.D: Ineffective breathing pattern with oxygen saturation at 85%

explanation: Airway and breathing always come first! Life-threatening issues take top priority over comfort, teaching, or emotional needs every single time.

question: What crucial warning must you give a patient prescribed benzonatate capsules?

options.A: Swallow the capsules whole without chewing.
options.B: Crush the pills and mix them into fruit juice.
options.C: Dissolve the capsule slowly on top of the tongue.
options.D: Open the capsule and rub the liquid on the throat.

explanation: Never let patients chew benzonatate! It will numb their mouth and throat so fast that they risk choking or aspiration.

question: Which tier of government in Nigeria has the primary responsibility for running grassroots primary healthcare?

options.A: Federal Government only
options.B: Traditional royal palaces
options.C: Local Government Areas
options.D: Private international donors

explanation: Local Government Areas (LGAs) are tasked with the daily grassroots delivery of PHC to our towns and villages.

question: Why does blood pressure fall in early and mid-pregnancy even though blood volume is rising?

options.A: Kidneys excrete all excess fluid immediately
options.B: The heart pumps with much less force
options.C: Blood vessels constrict to push blood to the lungs
options.D: Progesterone reduces systemic vascular resistance

explanation: Brilliant! Progesterone relaxes blood vessel walls so they widen, which naturally lowers resistance and blood pressure.

question: What are Cheyne-Stokes respirations?

options.A: Extremely fast breathing that remains constant until death occurs
options.B: A loud rattling sound caused by fluid trapped in the upper airway
options.C: Completely silent and shallow breathing with no obvious pattern
options.D: Deep, rapid breaths followed by temporary pauses in breathing

explanation: Cheyne-Stokes breathing has a distinct rhythm: the breaths get deeper and faster, then completely stop for a few seconds before starting again.

question: Why are older adults much more prone to chronic dehydration?

options.A: Kidneys produce excessive water during the night.
options.B: The natural sensation of thirst decreases with age.
options.C: Older adults require zero fluids to maintain normal health.
options.D: The skin absorbs all environmental moisture instantly.

explanation: Spot on! As people grow older, their internal thirst signals get quieter, meaning they might not feel thirsty even when their body is crying out for water.

question: Which group of professionals makes up the core mental health team?

options.A: Pharmacists, physiotherapists, and laboratory technicians
options.B: Surgeons, anesthetists, and theater nurses
options.C: Psychiatrists, nurses, social workers, and occupational therapists
options.D: Hospital administrators, accountants, and security officers

explanation: Spot on! Good mental health care brings together medical, nursing, social, and daily living expertise.

question: Why is it discouraged to repeat an overly studied topic without a new angle?

options.A: It fails to contribute meaningful new knowledge to nursing
options.B: It is illegal under international copyright laws
options.C: It automatically causes patients to reject treatment
options.D: It requires more expensive laboratory equipment

explanation: If we just copy old studies without adding anything new, we aren't helping evidence-based practice grow. Let's aim for fresh insights!

question: Which specific medication is the go-to emergency antidote for an opioid overdose?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Naloxone
options.D: Digoxin immune fab

explanation: Fantastic! Naloxone quickly blocks opioids and helps the patient breathe normally again. Keep this one locked in your memory!

question: What life-threatening emergency happens when fluid overload backs up all the way into the lungs?

options.A: Pleural mesothelioma
options.B: Chronic bronchial asthma
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Acute pulmonary edema

explanation: When the kidneys can't clear fluid, it backs up into the air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs, causing acute pulmonary edema and severe breathing distress. You're mastering critical care concepts!

question: Why do medications absorb very slowly from the dermal layer of the skin?

options.A: The epidermis blocks most medications from entering.
options.B: Sweat glands actively wash the medication away.
options.C: Skin cells in the dermis are tightly packed together.
options.D: The dermis has a very limited blood supply.

explanation: Limited blood vessels in the dermis mean the drug stays localized and is picked up very gradually by the body. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: How do vaccines primarily protect the human body against infectious diseases?

options.A: By lowering body temperature during an active viral infection
options.B: By destroying bacteria directly with heavy doses of antibiotics
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to produce protective antibodies
options.D: By cleaning harmful toxins directly out of the bloodstream

explanation: Vaccines teach the immune system to recognize and fight off specific germs safely. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient expresses deep worry that their life had no meaning and feels utterly forgotten. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Tell them not to worry because everyone feels sad sometimes
options.B: Sit quietly, listen attentively, and validate their feelings
options.C: Change the subject immediately to cheer them up
options.D: Administer a strong sedative to make them sleep

explanation: Allowing patients to voice deep spiritual or existential worries without judgment offers profound comfort. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h3)
